title: The PS5 hacking scene just took a big leap forward
gist: The new Relapse exploit jailbreaks any PS5 on firmware up to 13.6, using a WebKit vulnerability to gain kernel write access, vastly expanding the pool of hackable consoles and compatible games compared with prior exploits limited to old firmware.

insights.claim: The Relapse exploit can jailbreak any PS5 on firmware up to 13.6 (released in July), meaning any console not updated to the mid-September 14.00.00 firmware.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: A large installed base of consoles becomes jailbreakable, a security challenge for Sony's platform.
insights.quote: That means jailbreaking is now possible on any PS5 that was last updated before the mid-September release of firmware version 14.00.00.

insights.claim: Relapse uses a long-known WebKit vulnerability in the PS5 browser to escalate to kernel write access and install an ELF loader, and is far more efficient than earlier exploits that could hang the system for 50 minutes per attempt.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Unpatched browser-engine flaws remain a key attack surface for locked-down devices.

themes.theme: Expanded jailbreak market and homebrew use

insights.claim: Because most PS5 games require the firmware current at their release, compatibility with recent firmware makes the Relapse exploit work with many more titles.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Broader game compatibility increases piracy and backup risk for console software sales.

insights.claim: Previously, newcomers to PS5 hacking had to find older, unupdated consoles on the secondary market, but exploitable hardware availability is now greatly expanded.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Lower barriers to jailbreaking broaden the homebrew and piracy user base.
insights.quote: The overall availability of exploitable PS5 hardware is now greatly expanded.

insights.claim: Jailbroken PS5s can run homebrew emulators and unofficial 60 fps mods for PS4 games, while a full Linux implementation currently works only on firmware 7.61 or earlier.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Homebrew capabilities increase demand for unpatched hardware.
